description: Scale q and k by a constant 1.2 after QK RMS norm, sharpening attention logits by 1.44x.
Lower EMBEDDING_LR from 0.6 to 0.4 to test whether embedding updates are too aggressive.
Change WINDOW_PATTERN from "SSSL" to "SSSS" (last layer is still forced long by the code) to speed up attention and get more steps in the fixed time budget.
Change ADAM_BETAS from (0.8, 0.95) to (0.9, 0.95) to test whether more Adam momentum helps embeddings.
Set HEAD_DIM from 128 to 64, doubling the attention heads from 4 to 8 at the same width (n_head is derived as model_dim // HEAD_DIM, and FA3 supports head dim 64).
Reduce Muon cautious WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.1.
Halve TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**18 so grad accumulation drops from 8 to 4 and the run gets about twice as many optimizer steps in 300 s.

issues: (1) No integrity problem found. The diff only changes the per-step logging and fast-fail block. The seed lines, the prepare.py import, the data, the evaluation call and the final summary are untouched.

(2) No bug that would make the result meaningless. Calling train_loss.item() only every 20 steps removes a host-device sync from most steps, so the change can only affect throughput. The NaN/explosion check now runs only every 20 steps, so a diverging run can go up to 19 extra steps before it aborts. That does not affect val_bpb.

Minor: the logged 'loss' is now an EMA over every 20th step rather than every step, so printed loss values can't be compared directly with incumbent logs. The removed debiasing is handled by seeding the EMA at step 0, which assumes the step counter starts at 0. This affects console output only.

(3) The numbers are consistent. The candidate scored 1.0965 against the incumbent's 1.0981, a raw gain of 0.0016. With only 1 run on each side this is well within noise (reported z = 0.208, implying a noise scale of about 0.0077). The provisional reject matches the numbers. A speed-only change like this would need replicates or a tok/sec comparison to show a real gain.
z cannot be recomputed independently: the noise standard deviation is not given and there is only n=1 per arm. The reported z is consistent with the sign and size of the difference.

description: Only call loss.item() and print/log every 20 steps instead of every step, keeping the timing sync.
Reduce Muon Newton-Schulz iterations from 5 to 3 (ns_steps=3, same coefficients, dropping the last two) to cut optimizer overhead.
Raise MATRIX_LR from 0.04 to 0.05 for faster Muon progress in the short budget.
Set Muon cautious WEIGHT_DECAY from 0.2 to 0.0, since the model is underfit in a 300 s run.
Set DEPTH=6 and ASPECT_RATIO=96, giving model_dim 576 rounded up to 640 (5 heads of dim 128), for a shallower, wider and faster model.
Set WARMUP_RATIO from 0.0 to 0.02 so the learning rate ramps up linearly over the first 2% of the time budget.
Set WINDOW_PATTERN to "SSSS" and scale q and k by 1.2 after the QK RMS norm.
Add a 1e-4 * mean(logsumexp(logits)^2) z-loss to the training loss only, applied in forward when the model is in training mode.

issues: The diff only changes the Muon momentum schedule (warmup 300 -> 200 steps, final momentum 0.95 -> 0.9). It is a legitimate hyperparameter change: nothing touches the evaluation, data, seed lines or the prepare.py import.

z cannot be recomputed. There is 1 candidate run and 1 incumbent run, so neither side has a spread. The difference is 0.0025 (1.0956 vs 1.0981). The reported z=0.328 implies the harness used a noise sigma of about 0.0076 from an outside source.
The decision to reject is consistent with z=0.328. Given n=1 per arm, the 0.0025 gain is within plausible run-to-run noise. A replicate would be needed to confirm it.

Halve SCALAR_LR from 0.5 to 0.25 to stabilize the per-layer scalar parameters.
